text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing costs 1 but only returns 0.75 to self, though the group as a whole gains 3 per token contributed—so free-riding is individually dominant but full contribution is socially optimal. I'll lean toward a moderate-to-high contribution to balance cooperation with self-interest.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 3 total across the group but only 0.75 back to me, so the dominant strategy is to contribute nothing, yet full cooperation maximizes group payoff. I'll lean toward a moderate cooperative opening contribution, something like 10.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 3x to the group but only 0.75x to the individual contributor, making defection individually dominant despite cooperation being socially optimal. With 10 repeated rounds, though theory says selfishness dominates in a one-shot game and backward induction suggests the same in finite repetition, I'm weighing whether starting cooperatively could still build trust and boost collective payoff.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 60 in total, and you got 45 points.

reply.thinking: Confirming round 1 worked out: I kept 20, pool paid back 45, netting me a gain. For round 2, others averaged about 13 contributed, but I'll stay consistent and keep contributing 20 to maintain cooperation.
